newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to ask suppliers to cut car part prices.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to ask suppliers to cut car part prices.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Tuesday it would ask its suppliers to cut prices for parts to be supplied for its new models, but refused to say by how much.

The economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported earlier on Tuesday that Mazda had requested that its suppliers cut car part prices for Mazda's new Capella model and its future models by about 30 percent.
"We have been making efforts to reduce production costs," a Mazda spokeswoman said. "We have set a certain cost-reduction target for our products, but we do not want to disclose the details."
Mazda is expected to launch the Capella next month, industry sources said.
The daily said Mazda reviews its purchasing prices every six months, and asks its suppliers to cut their prices on some parts by three to five percent.
Other carmakers also usually revise their purchasing prices for existing car parts every six months.
The daily said they have also been seeking separate larger cuts in prices for parts for new models.
Mazda's domestic sales fell 3.5 percent year-on-year to 377,000 units in the year to March 1997 due to poor demand for almost all of its models, and to slow development of new recreational models.
But its Demio compact recreational model, which was launched in August last year, has been popular and helped the company post year-on-year gains in domestic sales in May and June.
Mazda is about one-third owned by Ford Motor Co.
